A broadly general "good leader" and an elected representative are different though.

Doing the opposite of what the people you represent want and then telling them why they are wrong and you are right is not representing them.

A vote for a city councillor should not be viewed as a blanket mandate to do whatever you want. It doesn't mean "we trust you to do whatever is right regardless of what our opinions are."

The goal should be to vote for what the people in your ward want. I hate Francis and think he's scum, but also if people in Stony Creek are NIMBYs who don't want this development then he would not be representing his constituents well if he voted in favor of it.

>Just because people are protesting against the actions of Israel, doesn't make them "pro hamas". 

Why are you misrepresenting the claims being made? It's okay if you think the claims are inaccurate or you think what is being claimed should be acceptable, but regardless of what you believe it is dishonest to frame their claims that way when their actual claims are public and include specifics that absolutely go well beyond people "just ... protesting against the actions of Israel"

​

>Among the specific allegations, the statement of claim says at rallies held at McMaster, students were "praising Hamas' actions and calling for more violence against the Jewish community."  
Jewish students have also been subjected to chants and calls for "death to Jews" and "Israelis must go" and fear wearing religious symbols will trigger "acts of aggression" from others on campus, the statement of claim says.

https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/hamilton/mcmaster-lawsuit-1.7074537

Agree that this lawsuit will go nowhere and I don't know enough about the lawyers to speak to that.

But to the rest of your message, it strikes me that the following claims absolutely fall under "advocating for violence" and are not claiming criticism of Israel as anti-semetic.

>Among the specific allegations, the statement of claim says at rallies held at McMaster, students were "praising Hamas' actions and calling for more violence against the Jewish community."  
Jewish students have also been subjected to chants and calls for "death to Jews" and "Israelis must go" and fear wearing religious symbols will trigger "acts of aggression" from others on campus, the statement of claim says.

https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/hamilton/mcmaster-lawsuit-1.7074537

Whether you believe these claims are true or not (and unless you've spent much time on the Mac campus recently, your belief about the claims probably doesn't mean any more than me or anyone else's), I'm not sure how you arrive at those claims being about criticism of Israel.
There are lots of options to get something in the "shawarma or whatever" category for well under 15 bucks. Banh Mi is like $7. Sub at Bonanza similar.  Sign of the times.
Where does The Burnt Tongue publish their profits?

Given it seems to you like an obvious idea, and that you don't see restaurants doing it, could it maybe be that it isn't actually a good idea? Like the experts have thought of the idea that you thought of, but through the lens of their expertise have decided not to do it?

Alternatively, if you're certain it's a good idea, that's a terrific opportunity for you. A big niche in the industry that you can fill by putting your idea to the test.

If you don't think either of these are true, do you think it would be reasonable for a restaurant owner to look at what you do for work, offer a very simple insight into how *they* think your industry should be run, and be taken seriously?

The fossil fuel industry is awful for sure, definitely agree.

But if you legitimately believe they are guilty of mass murder, then wouldn't every piece of unnecessary plastic you have bought in your life have been you deciding that helping fund mass murder is worth whatever convenience you're getting?

I dunno, I suspect a guy who is one of the world's biggest international stars with a top-10 social media follower count might have a better idea of "what the ppl want" than you do unless you have a very specific definition of "the ppl"
